fieldMarks: Heavy, flattened body with short stocky legs, short neck, broad head and short bushy tail; 26-35 in long, roughly 4-12 kg.
Brown face marked with a white stripe running back from the nose, white patches and vertical black bars; throat and chin whitish.
The white head stripe ends near the shoulders in northern animals but runs to the rump in southern ones.
Grayish to reddish back and flanks with a buffy belly; low, rounded ears.
behavior: Solitary and mainly nocturnal; less active in winter, passing it in bouts of torpor and emerging on warm days.
Catches most food by digging after pocket gophers, ground squirrels, prairie dogs, mice and voles; also eats rabbits, insects, reptiles and eggs.
Digs a series of dens across its home range; typical burrows are about 1 ft in diameter, leaving conspicuous holes and mounds.
habitat: Dry, open grasslands, prairies, fields and pastures, favouring sandy soils where burrowing prey is easy to dig out; from alpine meadows to below sea level.
range: Primarily the Great Plains: north into the central-western Canadian provinces, through suitable habitat across the western United States and south into Mexico; has expanded east since about 1900 and now reaches Ontario.
